description: Participants forecast with the discipline of a backtest. On synthetic daily electricity demand from Shams Power, a fictional distributor with 12 regions and 400 feeders, they decompose series, set a seasonal-naive benchmark floor, fit exponential smoothing and ARIMA-family models with weather and Hijri holidays, train one boosted model across many series, reconcile feeder and regional forecasts and run pretrained zero-shot forecasters as baselines. Every method is scored by rolling-origin cross-validation with point and probabilistic measures and reaches the planner as a fan chart.
audience: Specialists. Analysts and data scientists who have completed the level 200 set or can show equivalent work: an analysis or model they built, validated and can explain.
prerequisites: DS-204 Machine Learning for Tabular Data: Baselines and Validation
Resamples and reshapes time-indexed data in a dataframe

outcomes.text: Apply decomposition and a seasonal-naive benchmark floor scored by rolling-origin cross-validation, given regional daily demand with weekly and annual seasonality
outcomes.evidence: a backtest table of scaled errors by horizon

outcomes.text: Implement exponential smoothing, ARIMA-family and dynamic regression models with temperature and moving-holiday terms, given the regional series and a Hijri and Gregorian calendar
outcomes.evidence: residual diagnostics and scores against the floor

outcomes.text: Measure point and quantile accuracy of a global boosted model and a pretrained zero-shot forecaster against statistical models, given 400 feeder series with eight weeks held out
outcomes.evidence: a scorecard of scaled error, pinball loss, coverage, run time and licence terms

outcomes.text: Review a forecast evaluation for leakage across time and selection on the test window, and correct it, given a notebook with three seeded faults
outcomes.evidence: a review memo and a corrected backtest

outcomes.text: Build a forecasting analysis for new series and defend method, horizon and uncertainty to a planner, given a supplied dataset and a planner's request
outcomes.evidence: a repository and a two-page note with fan charts, defended live
